<!-- Generated by `node scripts/docs-reference.mjs`. Do not edit. -->

Every track has a Mute button and a Solo button in its header. Mute silences that track; Solo silences every other track so you hear this one alone. Both are listening aids only — they change what you hear while you work, and the export still renders every unmuted track.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **The Mute and Solo buttons in the track control panel**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-second-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
4. Press **Mute** in the track's header. The second track drops out of playback.
5. Press **Solo** in the track's header. Solo overrides mute on this track and silences every other one, so you hear the second loop on its own.

## Tips

- Press a button again to release it. **Tracks → Mute all tracks** clears every track at once.
- Solo several tracks to audition a group together; muting is then only needed for the odd one out.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
